Remodel the landscape; collect flowers and coins; step on snakes, worms and freak beasts; and fight flipping wars. All this in one game! The “Classic” version of Marram is a skilful strategic tile placement game for 2-4 players that is easy to learn, but difficult to master. Take turns laying 2 tiles that show body lengths of snakes and worms, and patches of grass and sand, laying them to fit with those already laid. Rather than laying a tile, you can remodel the landscape with a spade, flipping a tile that’s already been laid. You lay welly boots to claim control of features, such as snakes, worms, grass and sand patches and score points when the features are complete. Score more points than your opponents and you win! Learn how to play with the short game, which takes 15-25 minutes, and use these new skills in the long game (25-40 minutes) which is significantly more strategic Or pit your wits playing the more complex “Pitchfork” variant – a game of two halves. Capture and remove snakes and worms in the first part of the game, and fight for control over wide expanses of grass and sand in the remainder. You need to think deeply and strategically in the long version of the game which takes about an hour. The short game takes 25 to 35 minutes. Finally, a slightly nutty variant “Animals” expands on “Pitchfork” where you have a chance to bet on whether a fly and a frog get eaten by a snake to win bonus points. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary For tips on how to play marram, see Tips_marram Contents 1 How to play 1.1 Marram Classic 1.1.1 Place a tile 1.1.2 Flip a tile 1.2 Marram Pitchfork 2 Scoring 2.1 Marram Classic 2.2 Marram Pitchfork How to play Marram Classic Each turn, a player must do the following twice : place a tile; or flip a tile. Place a tile When placing a tile, all the features of adjacent tiles must match: grass tufts, sand, orange snakes, blue snakes and worms. If there are any remaining in their supply, a player may optionally place a welly boot on a feature of the placed tile. If the tile placement completes a feature, that feature scores for the player with the most welly boots on it. All welly boots from completed features are returned to their respective players. Flip a tile A player may only flip a tile if they have at least one remaining shovel in their supply. Flipping a tile expends a shovel from the player's supply. The player selects a tile with a shovel symbol on it and turns it over in place. If there are any welly boots on the flipped tile itself, they are removed from the game. The tile is then realigned, if necessary, so that its features match with the adjacent tiles. If more than one rotation is possible, the player may choose. The player may then optionally place a welly boot on a feature on the tile. Any features completed as a result of the flipping are scored, including those from welly boots just placed. Welly boots from completed features are returned to their owners. Marram Pitchfork Same as classic, except with using pitchforks for claiming the creatures. A completed creature will disappear from the board, making it much easier to complete grass tufts and sand mounds. Pitchforks will be returned to their owners for each completed creature. Scoring Marram Classic Completed features Type of feature Conditions Scoring Orange snake Must have two ends . 1 point for each end, plus 1 point for each middle segment. Worm Must have two ends and one saddle . 2 points for each end, 2 points for the saddle, plus 2 point for each middle segment. Blue snake Must have one head , one tail and at least one middle segment . 3 points for the head, 3 points for the tail, plus 3 points for each middle segment. Freak beasts Any worm or snake that fails to meet its species criteria 3 points. [Rating: 1/10] One of the ugliest game I have ever seen, it's simply a bad rip-off of Carcassonne.

[Rating: 2/10] + Carcassonne-esque blocking opportunities and teasing opponent by creating freaks -- awful and distracting colour mix -- ugly to the eye -- gameplay feels frustrating more often than not

[Rating: 2/10] I really didn't enjoy this game. It just feels far too long for me and I had far too many turns where I didn't feel like I had any decent moves. The goals and turn structure of the game were fine, but I really disliked the game arc.

[Rating: 3/10] I don't see what the point of this game is.  It's basically just a bad version of Carcassonne.  At least Carcassonne has a ton of expansions that you can mix and match.

[Rating: 3/10] Digital.  Carcassonne knockoff and long and tough to complete things.  I have never heard a fellow Brit or anyone but the "designer" call it "Welly Boot"?  Wellington Boot! Painful and for 15 min short game, has taken 90 minutes
